questions.question: Who has the power to recommend President's Rule in a state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Governor** of a state has the constitutional authority under **Article 356** of the **Indian Constitution** to recommend the imposition of **President’s Rule** (also known as State Emergency).
 
• This recommendation is made when the **Governor** is satisfied that the government of the state cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the **Constitution**, signifying a breakdown of constitutional machinery.
 
• While the **President** is the authority who officially issues the proclamation, they generally act based on a formal report submitted by the **Governor**, though the President can also act independently if a grave situation arises.
 
• Upon the imposition of **President’s Rule**, the **Council of Ministers** headed by the **Chief Minister** is dismissed, and the state administration comes under the direct control of the **Union Government** through the **Governor**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Framework**:

 
 
• **Article 356**: Inspired by **Section 93** of the **Government of India Act, 1935**, it allows the Center to take over state administration.
 
• **Parliamentary Approval**: Every proclamation of **President’s Rule** must be approved by both houses of **Parliament** within **two months** (60 days) by a **simple majority**.
 
• **Duration**: Once approved, it continues for **six months** and can be extended up to a maximum of **three years** with periodic parliamentary approval every six months.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Oversight**:
 
 
• **S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994)**: A landmark **Supreme Court** judgement that established the power of **judicial review** over the President’s proclamation to prevent the arbitrary dismissal of state governments.
 
• The court ruled that the **floor test** in the **State Legislative Assembly** is the only valid way to check the majority of a government.
 
 
 
• **Related Emergency Provisions**:
 
 
• **Article 352**: Relates to **National Emergency** due to war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.
 
• **Article 360**: Relates to **Financial Emergency**, which has never been declared in India to date.

questions.question: Who has the power to appoint the Chief Minister when no party has a clear majority in the State Assembly?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Article 164** of the **Constitution of India**, the **Chief Minister** is appointed by the **Governor** of the state.
 
• While the Governor normally appoints the leader of the party that secures a majority in the **State Legislative Assembly**, they exercise **situational discretion** when no single party or alliance has a clear majority.
 
• In the event of a **hung assembly**, the Governor is responsible for appointing a person who is most likely to command the **confidence of the house** to ensure a stable government.
 
• The Governor generally invites the leader of the **single largest party** or a **post-poll alliance** to form the ministry and prove their majority on the floor of the house through a **vote of confidence**.
 
• This discretionary power is a vital constitutional function meant to prevent a **constitutional breakdown** or political instability within the state executive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **President**:

 
 
• The **President of India** appoints the **Prime Minister** under **Article 75** but does not have the authority to appoint a State Chief Minister.
 
• The President acts as the **nominal head** of the Union, whereas the Governor acts as the nominal head of the state.
 
 
 
• **Speaker of the Assembly**:
 
 
• The **Speaker** is the **presiding officer** of the **Vidhan Sabha**, elected by its members.
 
• The Speaker’s role is limited to legislative proceedings and maintaining house decorum; they hold no executive power to appoint the **Chief Minister**.
 
 
 
• **Prime Minister**:
 
 
• The **Prime Minister** is the real executive head of the **Union Government**.
 
• While the PM may influence political decisions through the party hierarchy, the **Constitution** does not grant the PM any formal power in the appointment process of a **Chief Minister**.

questions.question: According to the historical overview, what elements must be understood first to study the history of Indian music?

options.text: Human origin and elements like sound, tone, and rhythm

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Human origin and elements like sound, tone, and rhythm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To study the **history of Indian music**, one must trace back to the **human origin**, as music is intrinsically linked to the biological and psychological development of mankind.
 
• The fundamental element of music is **Nada (Sound)**; ancient Indian musicology identifies it as the primordial vibration from which the universe emerged, often termed **Nada Brahma**.
 
• **Swar (Tone)** is the melodic foundation that differentiates musical sound from noise; historical study begins with how humans transitioned from **monotone vocalizations** to the structured **Sama Veda** chants.
 
• **Laya (Rhythm)** represents the temporal aspect of music, derived from natural phenomena like the **heartbeat** or the **seasons**, which provided the first rhythmic frameworks for early humans.
 
• Understanding these three pillars (**Sound, Tone, and Rhythm**) is essential before analyzing the complex **Raga-Tala** systems found in texts like the **Natya Shastra** by **Bharat Muni**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Analysis of Related Concepts**:

 
 
• **Human Evolution and Technical Skills**: While **technical skills** are necessary for instrument making, they are considered secondary developments that occurred after the realization of vocal **tone** and **rhythm**.
 
• **Civilization and Language**: **Language** is a medium of literal communication, whereas music is a **universal language of sound** that existed prior to the formalization of scripts and complex grammars.
 
• **Instruments and Dance**: In the classical definition of **Sangeetam** (Gitam Vadyam tatha Nrityam), **Gitam** (vocal/sound) is the primary element that directs the **Vadyam** (instruments) and **Nrityam** (dance).
 
 
 
• **Historical Foundations**:
 
 
• **Shruti**: The history of Indian music relies on the **22 Shrutis** (microtones), which are the smallest audible frequencies perceived by the human ear.
 
• **Vedic Music**: The transition from **Archik** (one note) and **Gathik** (two notes) to **Samik** (three notes) represents the earliest **tonal history** of the Indian subcontinent.

questions.question: The Malwa Plateau is primarily located in which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Malwa Plateau** is a prominent physiographic division of India located in the **west-central** part of the country, primarily occupying the western region of **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• Geologically, the plateau is of **volcanic origin** and forms a part of the **Deccan Traps**, which were created by **fissure eruptions** of basaltic lava during the **Cretaceous period**.
 
• The region is bounded by the **Vindhya Range** to the south and the **Madhya Bharat Pathar** and **Bundelkhand** to the north and northeast, serving as a transitional landform between the **Indo-Gangetic Plain** and the **Deccan Plateau**.
 
• The plateau is characterized by a **rolling surface** with an average elevation ranging between **500 to 600 meters** above sea level, sloping generally towards the **north** and **northeast**.
 
• The drainage system of the plateau includes major rivers such as the **Chambal**, **Kali Sindh**, **Shipra**, **Parbati**, and **Betwa**, all of which eventually join the **Yamuna** or the **Ganga**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Soil and Agriculture:**

 
 
• The plateau is covered with fertile **Black Soil** (also known as **Regur soil**), which is highly moisture-retentive and rich in **iron** and **magnesium**.
 
• This soil type makes the region a hub for the production of **Soybean**, **Wheat**, **Cotton**, and **Gram**.
 
 
 
• **Regional Extensions:**
 
 
• **Rajasthan:** While primarily in Madhya Pradesh, the southeastern portion of Rajasthan, known as the **Hadoti region** (including Kota, Bundi, and Jhalawar), is a part of this plateau system.
 
• **Gujarat and Maharashtra:** These states share boundaries with the plateau region but do not house the primary expanse of the **Malwa** landform itself.
 
 
 
• **Climate:** The region experiences a **tropical climate** with moderate temperatures, largely influenced by its inland location and elevation.

questions.question: The Bhabar zone is associated with which physiographic feature of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Himalayan foothills**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bhabar** is a narrow belt ranging between **8 to 16 km** in width, lying parallel to the **Shiwalik foothills** at the break-of-slope.
 
• It is the northernmost stretch of the **Indo-Gangetic Plain**, forming the transition zone where the **Himalayan rivers** descend from the mountains and deposit heavy materials.
 
• The region is characterized by the accumulation of **pebbles**, gravel, and rock debris, making the soil structure extremely porous.
 
• Due to this high **porosity**, smaller **rivers and streams disappear** underground in this zone, flowing beneath the surface of the pebble-studded bed.
 
• The **Bhabar** belt extends from the **Indus** river in the west to the **Teesta** river in the east, marking the edge of the **extra-peninsular** mountain system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terai Region**:

 
 
• Located south of the **Bhabar** belt, where the underground streams re-emerge on the surface.
 
• It is a **wet, swampy, and marshy** zone characterized by thick forest cover and high biological diversity.
 
 
 
• **Bhangar**:
 
 
• It represents the **older alluvium** of the **Northern Plains**, situated above the flood level of the rivers.
 
• The soil in this region often contains **calcareous deposits** known as **Kankar**.
 
 
 
• **Khadar**:
 
 
• It consists of **newer, younger alluvium** deposits found in the lower floodplains.
 
• This soil is extremely **fertile** and is naturally replenished every year by river floods, making it ideal for intensive farming.
 
 
 
• **Peninsular Plateau**:
 
 
• This is the oldest landmass of India, composed of **igneous and metamorphic rocks** like granite and gneiss, distinct from the alluvial deposits of the **Himalayan foothills**.

questions.question: The Global Liveability Index is released by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Economist Intelligence Unit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Global Liveability Index** is an annual report published by the **Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU)**, which provides a comprehensive assessment of the living conditions in **173 global cities**.
 
• The index measures the relative comfort for residents based on **30 qualitative and quantitative factors** divided across five distinct categories.
 
• The evaluation framework includes **Stability** (25%), **Healthcare** (20%), **Culture and Environment** (25%), **Education** (10%), and **Infrastructure** (20%).
 
• Each city is assigned a rating between **1 and 100**, where a score of **100** represents ideal living conditions and a score of **1** represents intolerable conditions.
 
• The report is widely used by multinational corporations to determine relocation packages and **hardship allowances** for expatriates moving to different urban centers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU)**:

 
 
• Established in **1946**, it is the research and analysis division of **The Economist Group**.
 
• In addition to liveability, it is well-known for producing the **Democracy Index** and various **World Cost of Living** reports.
 
 
 
• **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**:
 
 
• This agency is responsible for publishing the **Human Development Index (HDI)**, which ranks countries based on health, education, and income levels.
 
• It focuses primarily on ending poverty, reducing inequalities, and building resilience to achieve **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.
 
 
 
• **World Economic Forum (WEF)**:
 
 
• An international non-governmental organization based in **Cologny, Switzerland**, famous for its annual meeting in **Davos**.
 
• It publishes critical global assessments such as the **Global Competitiveness Report**, **Global Gender Gap Report**, and **Global Risks Report**.
 
 
 
• **World Bank**:
 
 
• A global financial institution that provides loans and grants to the governments of low- and middle-income countries.
 
• It regularly publishes the **World Development Report** and the **Global Economic Prospects** report.

questions.question: What year did World Archery become officially recognized by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) as the international governing body for archery?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1932**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **World Archery** was originally established as the **Fédération Internationale de Tir à l'Arc (FITA)** on **September 4, 1931**, in **Lwow, Poland** (now Lviv, Ukraine).
 
• The federation was founded by seven nations: **France**, **Czechoslovakia**, **Italy**, **Hungary**, **Poland**, **Sweden**, and the **United States of America**.
 
• The **International Olympic Committee (IOC)** officially recognized **FITA** as the international governing body for archery in **1932**, granting it authority over the sport's regulations and its role within the **Olympic Movement**.
 
• The primary objective of the federation at its inception was to create standardized international rules and competition formats to facilitate the return of archery to the **Olympic Games** program.
 
• Upon its recognition, **FITA** became responsible for the technical management of the sport, including the organization of the **World Archery Championships**, the first of which was held in **1931** with 21 competitors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Olympic Reinstatement (1972)**:

 
 
• While the governing body was recognized in **1932**, archery did not return to the **Olympic program** until the **Munich 1972 Games**.
 
• Before this 52-year hiatus, archery had been featured in the **1900**, **1904**, **1908**, and **1920** Olympics.
 
 
 
• **Organization Evolution**:
 
 
• The federation is headquartered in **Lausanne, Switzerland**, the same city as the **IOC** headquarters.
 
• In **2011**, the organization officially rebranded from **FITA** to **World Archery** during its **49th Congress** in **Turin, Italy**.
 
• Today, it oversees more than **160 member associations** and manages major events such as the **Archery World Cup** and the **World Archery Para Championships**.

questions.question: An engineer is assigned to monitor Earth's surface changes using radar, even through clouds and at night.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NISAR**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **NISAR** stands for **NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar**, which is a joint Earth-observing mission between the **National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)** and the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**.
 
• The mission utilizes **Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR)** technology, which works by transmitting microwave signals and measuring the reflection. Since microwaves can penetrate **atmospheric moisture**, the satellite can monitor Earth's surface through **clouds**, fog, and smoke.
 
• As an active sensor system, **SAR** provides its own source of illumination, allowing the satellite to capture high-resolution imagery during both **day and night**, independent of solar light.
 
• It is the first satellite mission to employ **dual frequencies**, specifically the **L-band** (provided by NASA) and the **S-band** (provided by ISRO), to observe subtle changes in Earth's surface.
 
• The primary scientific objective is to track **crustal deformation**, ice-sheet collapses, and changes in **terrestrial biomass**, mapping the entire globe once every **12 days**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandrayaan-3**

 
 
• This was India's third **lunar exploration mission** designed to demonstrate a soft landing on the **lunar south pole**.
 
• It successfully deployed the **Vikram lander** and **Pragyan rover** to conduct chemical analysis of the lunar surface.
 
 
 
• **XPoSat**
 
 
• The **X-ray Polarimeter Satellite** is India's first dedicated mission to study the **polarization** of cosmic X-rays.
 
• It targets high-energy celestial entities such as **black holes**, **neutron stars**, and **pulsar wind nebulae** using its payloads, **POLIX** and **XSPECT**.
 
 
 
• **EOS-09**
 
 
• This is part of ISRO's **Earth Observation Satellite** series intended for applications like **agriculture**, forestry, and **disaster management** support.
 
• While these satellites provide critical data, **NISAR** is the specific collaborative radar-focused mission described in the scenario.

questions.question: Which Indian rocket is called “Fat Boy”?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**GSLV MK III**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **GSLV Mk III** (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle Mark III) is the most powerful and heaviest launch vehicle designed and operated by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**.
 
• It earned the nickname **'Fat Boy'** due to its massive lift-off weight of approximately **640 tonnes** and its distinctively bulky appearance, primarily caused by the two large **S200 solid strap-on boosters**.
 
• The rocket is a **three-stage vehicle** comprising two solid propellant boosters, a core liquid propellant stage (L110), and a powerful **cryogenic upper stage (C25)** featuring the indigenous **CE-20 engine**.
 
• It is engineered to carry **4-tonne class** satellites into **Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO)** and roughly **10 tonnes** to **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)**.
 
• This launch vehicle was instrumental in India's major space milestones, including the **Chandrayaan-2** mission in **2019** and the successful **Chandrayaan-3** lunar landing mission in **2023**.
 
• ISRO has recently rebranded the GSLV Mk III as **LVM3** (Launch Vehicle Mark III) to signify its versatility in reaching various orbits beyond just the geosynchronous orbit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **PSLV**:

 
 
• Known as the **'Workhorse of ISRO'**, the **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle** is a highly reliable, medium-lift four-stage rocket.
 
• It is primarily used to deliver satellites into **Sun-Synchronous Polar Orbits** and was used for the **Mangalyaan** (Mars Orbiter) and **Chandrayaan-1** missions.
 
 
 
• **ASLV**:
 
 
• The **Augmented Satellite Launch Vehicle** was a five-stage solid fuel rocket developed to increase payload capacity to **150 kg** for LEO.
 
• It served as a crucial technology demonstrator during the late **1980s** and early **1990s** before the advent of PSLV.
 
 
 
• **SSLV**:
 
 
• The **Small Satellite Launch Vehicle** (mistyped as SSLP in options) is designed for **on-demand** launches of small satellites weighing up to **500 kg**.
 
• It aims to provide low-cost access to space with a quick turnaround time of only **72 hours** for integration.

questions.question: Which policy gave a major thrust to small-scale industries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1977 Industrial Policy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **1977 Industrial Policy** was announced by the **Janata Party Government**, marking a significant departure from the previous emphasis on heavy industries towards **employment-oriented** growth.
 
• It gave a major thrust to the **small-scale sector**, **cottage industries**, and **village industries** to promote **decentralized industrialization** and rural development.
 
• The policy introduced the concept of the **Tiny Sector**, targeting units with low investment in machinery and equipment to support the smallest entrepreneurs.
 
• A crucial institutional mechanism introduced was the **District Industries Centers (DICs)**, designed to provide all integrated services and support to small-scale industries at the district level under a **single roof**.
 
• The number of items reserved exclusively for the **small-scale sector** was drastically increased from 180 to **807 items** to protect them from competition with large-scale units.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1948 Industrial Policy:**

 
 
• This was the **first industrial policy** of independent India, which established the framework for a **Mixed Economy**.
 
• It classified industries into four categories: Strategic, Key, Important, and Other industries.
 
 
 
• **1956 Industrial Policy:**
 
 
• Known as the **Economic Constitution of India**, it was based on the **Mahalanobis Model** of development.
 
• It prioritized the **Public Sector** and the development of **heavy and basic industries**.
 
 
 
• **1980 Industrial Policy:**
 
 
• This policy aimed to promote the concept of **Economic Federation** and focused on **industrial licensing liberalization**.
 
• It sought to increase **productivity** and correct the distortions introduced by previous policy regimes while re-emphasizing the 1956 resolution.

questions.question: The first oil refinery in India was set up at:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Digboi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first oil refinery in India was established at **Digboi**, located in the **Tinsukia district** of **Assam**, and was commissioned on **December 11, 1901**.
 
• It was set up by the **Assam Oil Company Limited** following the discovery of crude oil in the region in **1889**, marking the beginning of the organized petroleum industry in India.
 
• **Digboi** is famously known as the **Oil City of Assam** and holds the distinction of being the **oldest operating oil refinery in Asia** and one of the oldest in the world.
 
• The refinery was established to process crude oil sourced from the **Digboi oil field**, which was the first commercially productive oil field in the **Indian subcontinent**.
 
• Today, the refinery is a unit of the **Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL)**, specifically under its **Assam Oil Division**, and continues to produce a wide range of petroleum products.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Haldia**

 
 
• Located in **West Bengal**, this refinery was commissioned in **1975**.
 
• It plays a vital role in supplying petroleum products to the **Eastern** and **North-Eastern** parts of India.
 
 
 
• **Koyali**
 
 
• Commonly known as the **Gujarat Refinery**, it is situated near **Vadodara** and was established in **1965**.
 
• It was built with technical assistance from the **Soviet Union** and is currently one of the largest refineries operated by **IOCL**.
 
 
 
• **Barauni**
 
 
• Situated in the **Begusarai district** of **Bihar**, it was commissioned in **1964**.
 
• This refinery was also developed in collaboration with the **USSR** and **Romania** to process crude oil from the **Naharkatiya** and **Moran** oil fields in Assam.

questions.question: When nominal Gross Domestic Product (GDP) rises faster than real GDP, it indicates:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**High inflation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nominal Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** measures the total value of all goods and services produced within a country at **current market prices**, meaning it accounts for both changes in production volume and changes in prices.
 
• **Real GDP** measures the economic output adjusted for price changes (inflation or deflation) by using **constant prices** from a designated **base year**, providing a clearer picture of actual production growth.
 
• The divergence between these two metrics is captured by the **GDP Deflator**, a price index calculated as ({Nominal GDP} / {Real GDP}) times 100 , which serves as a broad measure of **inflation**.
 
• When **Nominal GDP** rises faster than **Real GDP**, the growth in the nominal figure is not solely due to increased output but is heavily influenced by a significant rise in the **general price level**.
 
• This scenario directly indicates **High inflation**, as the cost of goods and services is increasing rapidly, causing the nominal value of the economy to swell even if the physical quantity of goods produced remains relatively stable or grows slowly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inflation and Deflation**:

 
 
• **Deflation**: Characterized by a general decline in prices; in this case, **Real GDP** growth would typically exceed **Nominal GDP** growth.
 
• **Falling Inflation**: Often called **disinflation**, this refers to a reduction in the rate at which prices increase, rather than a total decline in price levels.
 
 
 
• **Economic Growth Metrics**:
 
 
• **Zero Growth**: A state where the **Real GDP** remains constant over time, indicating no improvement in the country's productive capacity or standard of living.
 
• **Purchasing Power**: During periods of high inflation, the **purchasing power** of the domestic currency declines, requiring more money to buy the same amount of goods as in the previous year.

questions.question: What is the main drawback of India's trade balance?

options.text: Overdependence on a few trading partners
Persistent trade deficit due to imports

questions.question: Which social development scheme has been approved for an amount of Rs. 450 Crores from the years 2021-22 to 2025-26?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PM-DAKSH Scheme**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **PM-DAKSH (Pradhan Mantri Dakshta Aur Kushalta Sampann Hitgrahi)** Yojana is a **Central Sector Scheme** launched by the **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment** in **2020-21**.
 
• The government has approved the implementation of this social development scheme for the period **2021-22 to 2025-26** with a total financial outlay of **Rs. 450.25 Crores**.
 
• The primary objective of the scheme is to enhance the **competency levels** of the target groups to make them employable for both **self-employment** and **wage-employment**.
 
• The target beneficiaries include **Scheduled Castes (SCs)**, **Other Backward Classes (OBCs)** with annual income below Rs. 3 Lakh, **Economically Backward Classes (EBCs)**, **De-notified Tribes (DNTs)**, and **Safai Karamcharis**.
 
• Training programs offered under the scheme include **Up-skilling/Reskilling**, **Short-term Training**, **Entrepreneurship Development Programs**, and **Long-term Training**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **SMILE Scheme**:

 
 
• Stands for **Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise**.
 
• It has been allocated an outlay of **Rs. 365 Crore** for the period **2021-22 to 2025-26**.
 
• The scheme focuses on the **comprehensive rehabilitation** of **transgender persons** and persons engaged in the act of **begging**.
 
 
 
• **NAMASTE Scheme**:
 
 
• Stands for **National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem**.
 
• This initiative aims to ensure **zero fatalities** in sanitation work in India and provide **sustainable livelihoods** for sanitation workers.
 
 
 
• **Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan**:
 
 
• Launched on **August 15, 2020**, this campaign aims to address the issue of **drug abuse**.
 
• It focuses on **community mobilization** and **awareness generation** in vulnerable districts across the country.

questions.question: In which of the following places was Bahadur Shah Zafar sent to prison after the Revolt of 1857?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rangoon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bahadur Shah Zafar**, the last ruler of the **Mughal Dynasty**, was proclaimed the symbolic leader of the **Revolt of 1857** by the rebel Indian sepoys.
 
• After British forces successfully recaptured **Delhi** in **September 1857**, the emperor was apprehended by **Major William Hodson** at **Humayun’s Tomb**.
 
• Following his capture, he was tried at the **Red Fort** for his involvement in the uprising and was subsequently convicted of treason and conspiracy against the **British Crown**.
 
• In **1858**, the British authorities exiled him to **Rangoon** (modern-day **Yangon**) in **Burma** (now **Myanmar**), effectively terminating the Mughal Empire.
 
• He remained in confinement in **Rangoon** until his death on **November 7, 1862**, at the age of 87, and was buried there.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Andaman Islands**:

 
 
• These islands became infamous for the **Cellular Jail** (Kala Pani), where the British exiled many political prisoners, including **V.D. Savarkar**, but it was not used for the last Mughal Emperor.
 
 
 
• **Dhaka**:
 
 
• A prominent city in the **Bengal Presidency**, **Dhaka** was an important administrative and manufacturing center but did not serve as a place of exile for **Bahadur Shah Zafar**.
 
 
 
• **Shanghai**:
 
 
• A major port in **China**, **Shanghai** was a site of British commercial interest following the **Opium Wars**, but it had no historical involvement in the detention of leaders from the **1857 revolt**.
 
 
 
• **Poetic Legacy**:
 
 
• An accomplished **Urdu poet**, **Zafar** composed many verses expressing his grief and longing for his homeland during his years of exile in **Burma**.

questions.question: In which year did Atal Bihari Vajpayee became Prime Minister of India for the first time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1996**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Atal Bihari Vajpayee** served as the **10th Prime Minister of India** and assumed the office for the first time in **1996**.
 
• Following the **11th General Elections** held in **May 1996**, the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** emerged as the single largest party in the **Lok Sabha** with **161 seats**.
 
• President **Shankar Dayal Sharma** invited Vajpayee to form the government, and he was sworn in on **May 16, 1996**.
 
• His first tenure is historically significant for being one of the shortest in Indian history, lasting only **13 days**.
 
• Vajpayee resigned on **June 1, 1996**, after failing to secure support from other regional parties to prove a majority before a **vote of confidence** could take place.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subsequent Tenures**:

 
 
• He served a second term from **1998 to 1999** (13 months) and a third full term from **1999 to 2004**.
 
• He was the first non-Congress Prime Minister to complete a full **five-year term** in office.
 
 
 
• **Major Achievements**:
 
 
• He oversaw the **Pokhran-II** nuclear tests in **May 1998**, establishing India as a nuclear-armed state.
 
• He launched the **Golden Quadrilateral** project to connect major Indian metros via high-speed highways.
 
• He led the country during the **Kargil War** of **1999** against Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Honors and Legacy**:
 
 
• He was conferred with the **Bharat Ratna**, India's highest civilian award, in **2015**.
 
• His birth anniversary, **December 25**, is celebrated across India as **Good Governance Day**.
